terms.comment: Greek ὕμνος. Rare before the Christian writers; Augustine defines it as a song with the praise of God (hymnus cantus est cum laude Deī, Enarr. in Ps. 148.17, Lewis & Short). The hymns of Ambrose and Prudentius are still sung.

evidence: Aug. Conf. 9.6.14: in hymnīs et canticīs tuīs
terms.comment: In comedy the sung part of a play; in the Church a canticle, a song of Scripture outside the Psalms, such as the Magnificat.

phrases.latin: Et hymnō dictō, exiērunt in montem Olīvētī.
phrases.english: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

phrases.latin: tunc hymnī et psalmī ut canerentur secundum mōrem orientālium partium, nē populus maerōris taediō contābēsceret, īnstitūtum est
phrases.english: then it was laid down that hymns and psalms should be sung after the custom of the eastern parts, so that the people should not waste away in weariness and grief

sources: Lewis & Short: hymnus · Lewis & Short: canticum
